title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a draft of the opening of 'Le groupe de Brauer II' (GB II, §1): the cohomological Brauer group of a regular or locally factorial integral scheme embeds into the Brauer group of its function field. Grothendieck's own section numbering here is 5.x. The next page goes on to Br of open subschemes of Spec Z via cohomology with supports, which is GB III material.

Setting: X is integral (the conditions of '5.1 a)'), with generic point eta: Spec K -> X, where K = k(eta). Write R*_X = g_* G_{m,eta} for the sheaf of invertible rational functions and Div_X for the étale sheaf of Weil divisors, i.e. the sum over codimension-one points x of (i_x)_* Z. When the strictly henselian local rings are factorial (for example X regular), the divisor sequence
0 -> G_m -> R*_X -> Div_X -> 0
is exact on the étale site. This is presumably (5.3).

Vanishing of H^1(X, Div_X). For each codimension-one point x, H^1(X, i_{x*} Z) injects into H^1(k(x), Z) = Hom_cont(Gal, Z) = 0. Hence H^1(X, Div_X) = 0, and so H^2(X, G_m) -> H^2(X, R*_X) is injective.

Second injectivity. Hilbert 90 gives R^1 g_* G_m = 0. The Leray spectral sequence for g then makes H^2(X, g_* G_m) -> H^2(eta, G_m) = Br(K) injective.

Consequences.
- Proposition 5.4: the composite H^2(X, G_m) -> Br(K) is injective. In particular H^2(X, G_m) is torsion.
- Corollary 5.5: since Br(X) ⊂ H^2(X, G_m), Br(X) -> Br(K) is injective, and Br(X) is identified with a subgroup of Br(K).
- Théorème 5.6: an attempted characterisation of Br(X) inside H^2(X, G_m). The claim is that xi lies in Br(X) iff some finite étale surjective (Galois if one likes) X' -> X kills xi. The crossed-out first version restricted this to X a local scheme.
errors: Théorème 5.6 as finally phrased (X an arbitrary préschéma) is false in the direction 'xi in Br(X) implies xi is killed by a finite étale surjective cover'. Take a complex K3 surface with Br nonzero. It is simply connected, so its only finite étale covers are disjoint unions of copies of X, which kill nothing. The direction is correct for X local (Azumaya algebras over a local ring are split by a finite étale local extension), which was the crossed-out formulation. Globally one needs étale-local splitting rather than a single finite étale cover.

The converse direction (killed by a finite étale Galois cover implies the class is in Br) is not immediate. Hochschild–Serre leaves an H^1(G, Pic X') contribution beyond the crossed-product part H^2(G, Gamma(X', G_m)). This needs an argument (for instance X local, or one of GB I's criteria); the page gives none.
Prop. 5.4's hypotheses are garbled by revisions ('X étant l'irréductible[?] de Prop. 7[?]'). The required hypotheses are X integral (normal) with factorial strict local rings.

ideas.what: Divisor exact sequence on the étale site and vanishing of H^1(X, Div_X) for locally factorial (strict) local rings
ideas.modern_name: Étale divisor sequence; injectivity of H^2(X,G_m) -> H^2(X, g_*G_m)
ideas.where_published: Le groupe de Brauer II, §1 (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas)

ideas.what: H^2(X,G_m) -> Br(K) injective for regular integral X; hence Br(X) ⊂ Br(K) and H^2 is torsion
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of Brauer group into Brauer group of function field (regular schemes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Auslander–Goldman (dimension ≤ 2 / regular rings, algebraic version); Grothendieck GB II in general

ideas.what: Characterisation of Br(X) ⊂ H^2(X,G_m) as classes killed by finite étale covers
ideas.modern_name: Br vs Br' problem; splitting of Azumaya algebras by finite étale covers over local rings
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck GB I (local case); Gabber, de Jong (Br = Br' for quasi-projective schemes)
ideas.where_published: GB I §1–2 (local splitting, Br ⊂ H^2 torsion, discussion of Br = Br')

deep.surprise_reason: This is a manuscript draft of material that appears in polished form in GB II §1 (and GB III for the next page). The only notable feature is a globally false draft statement (Théorème 5.6), which Grothendieck had partly restricted and then generalised in revision. It is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'X étant l'irréductible[?] de Prop.[?] 7[?]' is a marginal insertion whose reading is uncertain; it plausibly refers to X being integral / irreducible under the conditions of a previous proposition.
'H^2(X, R^*_X)': R*_X denotes the sheaf of invertible rational functions g_* G_{m,eta}.
'Br(X) s'identifie [mais] à un sous-groupe': 'mais' is crossed out; read 's'identifie à un sous-groupe du groupe de Brauer Br(K) du corps des fonctions K = k(eta) de X'.
